title: Investigate wrong assessment_line_items being created
description:
When investigating students being blocked to progress on Articles inside Alpha Read it was identified two `assessment_line_items` pointing to the same `component_resource_sourced_id`. Due to this, the recommendations list was showing the article as not started and ready to begin, even with the student have doing this in the past.

After fixing this specific article a query was ran to identify others:

```
SELECT 
    component_resource_sourced_id,
    COUNT(*) as occurrence_count
FROM assessment_line_items
where component_resource_sourced_id like 'article_%'
GROUP BY component_resource_sourced_id
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
ORDER BY occurrence_count DESC;
```

By the time this ticket was being created, 32 `component_resource_sourced_id` were found as being used per 2 or more `assessment_line_items` records.

An investigation should answer the following questions:

* Who and how can mange `assessment_line_items`?
* Who did the changes that lead into this problems?
* How we should be able to address the fixes to point them to the correct ones?

title: QTI Rate Limit
description:
We have noticed some unnecessary stress put on the QTI api. The trend was about 10k requests a minute with 90% of those calls erroring out. The nature of the calls appear to be going in a loop consistently consuming resources and increasing the potential of issues that may happen during an academic session.

# Proposal for Solution

* We have reached out to LAWI team to investigate to see if there is a specific reason for this behavior, and if we can help provide a remedy.
* We need to ensure students are not blocked, so we will setup rate-limit that can be turned on in case of emergency.
  * This PR sets up a feature-flag for rate limiting. If RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=true, the api will enforce the rate limit. This allows us to turn rate-limit on or off depending on needs.

## Message to LWAI (email copy)

`Learning with AI Team` is the owner of the content and the script running. We have asked for them the reasoning behind the script. They said they would investigate the issue.

![Screenshot 2025-10-02 at 18.16.34.png](https://uploads.linear.app/244af9a6-164a-4274-82f7-5a0db9b24231/f1412a8c-23d3-4f17-bfd5-d41282867401/98831d76-ab81-49fe-ad7c-d573e294553d)

# How to test this PR

The rate limit can be tested using the load testing factory setup in ./load-testing

1. With the app started cd ../load-testing
2. `npm i` & `npm run load-testing:breakpoint`
3. Watch the server logs and log the result

### Testing Checklist and Todos

- [X] Load testing with a breakpoint without a client
  -Basic test inside of the load testing directory in QTI. `npm run load:breakpoint`
  -Received error messages once breakpoint began hitting limits.

2 tests left

- [ ] test the rate limit with a client id
- [ ] tests the rate limit when flag is set to false

todos

- [ ] update environments with new variables
  - [ ] prod
  - [ ] stag
  - [ ] test(?)

This load test may freeze the server. If you see the terminal stop, just end the test and log the results. You should see 

`ERRO[0493] API request to assessment-itemsById failed: 429 Your Client App has made too many requests, please try again later. Maximum requests per 1000ms is 100.  source=console`

title: Caio's Dash
description:
**As an Admin,**
I want to have access to a simple internal admin page that helps us debug analytics issues,
so that I can quickly investigate and resolve problems without manually running multiple queries.

**Problem Today**

Currently, when investigating analytics issues, the team needs to manually query multiple tables:

* `caliper_raw_events`
* `processed_facts`
* `assessment_results`

This is cumbersome because there are two different flows for events:

1. **Caliper-driven flow**
   * Event comes from Caliper → creates `assessment_results` → creates `processed_facts`.
2. **Manual flow**
   * Owner manually creates `assessment_results` → triggers creation of `processed_facts` → sends Caliper events with `process = false`.

⚠️ `process = false` ensures records are not duplicated in our DB, but still propagates the event to external platforms.

---

### **Requirements**

#### Filters

The page should allow filtering queries by:

* Student email
* Time of the event
* Subject
* Event type
* Sensor

When applied, these filters should trigger queries to each table (`caliper`, `processed_facts`, `assessment_results`) so admins can quickly compare data across flows.

#### Data to Highlight

* `process = true/false` flags.
* IDs in `assessment_results` (some have prefixes that indicate flow type).
* Student’s org and location (to better understand potential timezone context).

#### Timezone Handling

* Provide an option to change the timezone of the query.
* Allow testing across different timezones, since this sometimes changes which events appear.

---

title: [419] urgent timeback issue - courses not marked as completed
description:
## Root Cause

* Enrollments were being **soft deleted (**`tobedeleted`) instead of having their **end date set**.
* This **hid completed courses instead of marking them as completed**, so Timeback UI and integrated apps did not recognize completion.
* Students continued repeating lessons even after reaching 100% since the course was not showing as completed for them.
* Correct process: use **Administration → Manage Enrollments → Mark as Completed**, which sets the `end_date`.

## Investigation Phase

* Checked existing logic in Timeback to determine how completion is evaluated.
* Confirmed with AlphaLearn that `end_date` is the property they use to determine completion.
* Observed that affected courses had no `end_date` set despite being 100% completed.
* Noticed enrollments were **soft deleted (**`tobedeleted`), revealing the root cause: someone (or something) was incorrectly marking them this way.

---

## Resolution Phase

* Verified whether the enrollments in the ticket were linked to this issue.
* Confirmed Timeback was **not responsible** for automatically soft deleting enrollments.
* Checked logs for signs of automated “tobedeleted” actions.
* Reviewed codebase to confirm if Timeback should auto-update `end_date` on completion (it should not).
* Reviewed internal documentation.
* Synced with the PowerPath team to discuss the current logic and confirm the final resolution.
* Discussed response to requester and finalized next steps.

### Final Resolution

1. **Admins/maintainers are responsible for marking courses as completed** using *Manage Enrollments → Mark as Completed* (sets `end_date` for integrations).
2. **Share documentation** clarifying course completion logic and workflows.
3. **Update UI language**: remove misleading “Complete!” message when 100% of lessons are done; instead direct students to speak with their guide.

title: [228] [229] [60178692] Alpha Read - cross-out feature request
description:
> Hello Team,
>
> **Calie Garrett has suggested a feature in the Alpha Read app:**
>
> The ability for students to cross-out text that they have determined is NOT relevant to the question that they are answering.
>
> This would allow them to use deductive reasoning to find the answer, rather than relying on searching for the correct answer in a wall of text.
>
> **Calie shared the following:**
>
> > Oftentimes it's visually helpful to be able to cross out information that students are trying to either ignore, is irrelevant, or is clearly not the correct answer.  So it's helpful to be able to cross out answer choices as well as text that students either want to ignore to visually keep from including.For example, if a question is asking for a student to identify the thesis of a text, students might want to be able to cross out sentences that they can tell are either supporting details or conclusion statements, that way they eliminate them visually from their available options. It's just as powerful of a tool as highlighting.You know how sometimes it's easier to identify what we DON'T want than it is what we do? 
>
> Currently, AlphaRead offers the ability to highlight text, using left click and drag.
>
> The ability to cross-out text (Or highlight in Red) could be added using right click and drag.
>

description:
**User Story**
As a **support team member**, I want **newly created issues in Linear Triage to be automatically categorized, labeled, and prioritized by an AI system** so that **triage becomes faster, more consistent, and we reduce duplicate/manual effort.**

---

**Details / How it should work**

* When a new issue is created in Triage, the AI must:
  * Determine the correct ticket type (Feature, Question, Task, Bug).
    * If already set, reevaluate to ensure accuracy.
  * Assign the correct labels (OOS).
  * Detect up to 5?? platform areas mentioned and label them accordingly.
  * Assess and assign priority:
    * **High** – Blocking students from progressing.
    * **Medium** – Students can continue, but experience is negatively affected.
    * **Low** – Cosmetic or quality-of-life issue only.
  * Identify and mark possibly related issues (OOO).

---

**Dependencies**

* Depends on \[[1ED-1236](https://linear.app/ae-studio/issue/1ED-1236)\].
* Baby step: [1ED-1423](https://linear.app/ae-studio/issue/ffc48e58-1430-4d53-9843-058d043575bb).

---

**Acceptance Criteria**

* AI suggests ticket type.
* AI suggests relevant platform areas.
* AI suggests priority based on description.
* AI adds related issues when applicable.
* Can be run manually by a human

User roles
